open_points.subject: model value universe
open_points.text:
A model is a value
of one of the models of `models`, whichever it is; every other value is
answered as no model.
open_points.question: Which runtime values count as models: only M01–M29 records, also enumerations, request and answer projections, subclasses of declared classes, or every value made with the same modeling framework?
options: Only instances of the exact declared record classes M01–M29
All generated model classes, including requests and answer projections, but not enumerations
Declared classes and their subclasses
Every instance of the underlying framework's base model class
open_points.default_guess: Treat every generated record, request and answer projection class as a model, including subclasses, and treat enumerations and unrelated framework models as non-models.

witness.initial: A service operation has built a project-card answer containing a personal-data display name, and a test release gives the caller a highest class below personal_data.
events: operations asks model_fields whether the answer and its nested values are models before classing their fields
operations applies the caller's disclosure-class limit
outcomes: The answer projection counts as a model, so its display-name field is found and the answer is refused whole
Only M01–M29 domain records count as models, so the projection is answered as no model and a careful implementation may miss the field or traverse it by a different rule
witness.observer: the service caller, which either receives a refusal or receives the answer

open_points.subject: model recognition dependency
open_points.text:
Nothing. It reads values of the models of `models` without naming any of
them.
open_points.question: What owned runtime fact lets model_fields recognize exactly the permitted model values, which module owns that fact, and in which direction does the dependency run?
options: models owns and exports a marker base or runtime interface that model_fields imports
model_fields owns a marker or registration protocol that generated models import or register with
model_fields imports a third-party base class and treats every instance of it as a model
model_fields uses structural or reflective detection without an explicit dependency
open_points.default_guess: Have models own an exported marker base shared by every generated model class, and have model_fields depend on that marker; do not accept unrelated third-party model instances.

open_points.subject: model_items capability contract
open_points.question: Is model_items the final exported capability, and what are its parameters, return type, field-item representation, failure behavior and unambiguous no-model result?
options: Return a tagged result distinguishing no-model from an ordered sequence of name/value pairs
Return None for a non-model and an ordered sequence, possibly empty, for a model
Raise or return an error for a non-model
Expose separate is_model and model_items capabilities
open_points.default_guess: Make model_items final and return None for a non-model and an immutable ordered sequence of name/value pairs for a model; an empty sequence then remains the valid answer for a zero-field model.

witness.initial: An audit entry for erasing old entries contains the zero-field NoSubject value.
events: owner_interface or service_api asks model_items for NoSubject while rendering or encoding the audit view
The same traversal later asks model_items about an ordinary non-model scalar
outcomes: A distinct no-model sentinel lets the caller encode NoSubject as an empty model and handle the scalar separately
An empty collection represents both cases, so the caller cannot tell the zero-field model from a non-model by model_fields' answer alone
witness.observer: the owner reading the audit view

open_points.subject: callers of model_fields
open_points.text:
takes a model's
  fields only from `model_fields`, and tells a model from any other value
  by `model_fields`' answer alone
open_points.question: Which exact exported symbol does each of operations, owner_sessions, service_api and owner_interface import from model_fields, and what are the corresponding module_internal edges?
options: Each of the four consumers directly imports model_items from model_fields
Consumers receive an injected port and have no direct model_fields import
Another facade imports model_items and the four consumers depend on that facade
The two owner_interface traversals use different exported capabilities
open_points.default_guess: Declare model_items as the sole export used here and add a direct model_fields → model_items import surface for each of operations, owner_sessions, service_api and owner_interface.

witness.initial: The Factory runs with strict_imports while generating operations from the local specification.
events: The generated operations code directly calls model_items
The projector resolves imports solely from declared module_internal entries and contract-signature types
outcomes: An explicit operations-to-model_fields entry naming model_items produces a usable import
Only the prose dependency on model_fields exists, so model_items is absent from the generated module and generation or validation fails

open_points.subject: declared field semantics
open_points.text:
Reading the declared fields of a model value — each field's name and value,
in the order the model declares them
open_points.question: What exactly is a declared field and its name/value: specification field order or framework order, external/alias name or Python attribute name, raw stored value or serialized value, and are computed, private or extra fields excluded?
options: Only specification-declared fields, in specification order, using contract names and raw values
All fields reported by the modeling framework, in its metadata order
Serialized fields and aliases in wire order
Public runtime attributes discovered reflectively
open_points.default_guess: Return only specification-declared fields in specification order, under their contract field names, with raw values; exclude computed, private and extra attributes.

witness.initial: A generated answer model has a runtime attribute name different from its public wire-field name.
events: service_api walks the answer through model_fields
service_api writes each returned field name and value into the wire answer
outcomes: Contract names are returned, so the client receives the declared wire field
Runtime attribute names are returned, so the client receives a different field name
